title: Air Canada: chatbot advice contradicted the fare policy
date_basis: Month of chatbot interaction; tribunal decision dated 2024-02-14.
organization: Air Canada
system: Website chatbot; model and architecture not established by the passages reviewed
what_happened: The tribunal describes a chatbot advising that bereavement fares could be requested retroactively, followed by employees saying they could not. The passenger sought the fare difference.
impact: The tribunal found negligent misrepresentation and mostly allowed the claim. Dentons’ February 15, 2024 summary reports an award of $650.88, essentially the fare difference; this amount is attributed to that secondary account because the complete primary disposition was not recovered.
response: The decision records Air Canada denying liability, disputing retroactive eligibility and seeking dismissal (paragraph 4). Dentons reports a February 2023 email saying the issue was noted for a chatbot update; that establishes an intention, not a verified completed fix.
response_status: Company position and acknowledgement recorded in tribunal decision

Conflicting advice should route to review before the traveler relies on it. This is a proposed control, not a finding about the unknown chatbot implementation.
